name: Stuffing materials
anchor: EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 element-migration limits, matched per row to the EN 71-3 material category or categories the row's scope spans, taken jointly with the US ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble-element limits (mandatory under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and the Mexican NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable soluble-element limits, which state the same measured quantity; the strictest value across that family binds each cell. Total-content law (CPSIA lead, RoHS, REACH Annex XVII, Canadian SOR coating limits) is carried as disclosed companion obligations and never as a published number.
native_basis: element migration from accessible toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material. This row's scope spans the Directive's Category I (dry, powder-like, granular fill) and Category III (fibre wadding, foam, discrete pellets) material forms; the stricter of the two, Category I, is published across the whole row.
native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from accessible toy material (EN 71-3, mg/kg of material) — the stricter of the two material-category limit sets this row's scope spans (Category I) is published across the whole row; a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
scope_note: Fill and filling materials used inside stuffed, soft and bean-bag toys: polyester and natural-fibre wadding, foam crumb and slab, plastic granulate and pellets, expanded-polystyrene micro-beads, ground shell, cereal and bean fill, and weighting sand. The row is anchored on EN 71-3 Category I because dry, powder-like and granular fills are squarely within its scope; where the fill is a scraped-off-type material (fibre wadding, foam, discrete pellets) the Directive's Category III values would apply to that component and are looser, so HMTc publishes the stricter Category I ceiling across the whole row. That is a strictest-applicable selection within one instrument, not a blend of two.
material: Loose fill: fibre wadding, foam, granulate, pellets, micro-beads, ground shell, cereal/bean fill, weighting sand.
components: One test portion per distinct fill material and per distinct colour of dyed fill. Sample the fill as supplied inside the finished toy, not the pre-production lot. Where a toy contains a weighting pouch, the pouch fabric routes to toys-stuffed-bean-bag and the weighting medium is tested here.
basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III|I)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
basis_guard_note: This row's defining material form is dry, powder-like or granular fill, which is EN 71-3 Category I, but its scope also contains scraped-off-type fill (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets), which is Category III. The guard therefore admits the Directive's Category I AND Category III rows — both are genuinely applicable to material within this row's scope — and both are named on every cell so the strictest binds rather than the category label deciding the number. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum in the row's native basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; never occurrence-derived). Category 21 publishes on the element-migration basis only, pooling the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments, with each row pinned to the EN 71-3 material category or categories its scope actually spans.

Pb.basis: element MIGRATION from accessible toy material (EN 71-3, mg/kg of material) — the stricter of the two material-category limit sets this row's scope spans (Category I) is published across the whole row; a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum across the material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 2.0 mg/kg for Category I (this row's dry, powder-like and granular fill) and 23 mg/kg for Category III (its fibre wadding, foam slab and discrete pellets), against 90 mg/kg under ASTM F963-17 and 90 mg/kg under NOM-252-SSA1-2011. The Category I value binds at 2.0 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 as introduced by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 caps lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) at 1 mg/kg in the homogeneous material of consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles. Fill enclosed inside a toy is neither, so entry 72 is not read across as this row's ceiling; where a fibre fill is also supplied as a loose skin-contact textile, entry 72 binds it directly on a total-content basis and is a companion obligation. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans two of the Directive's material categories and the stricter of the two is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category III material forms (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling, and the compiled record's candidate set discloses both category values. STRUCTURAL NOTE: the durable fix is to split this row into per-material-category sub-rows, each with its own basis and its own Directive category. That requires new Category 21 subcategory slugs in data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json, which is a Step 0 taxonomy lock and outside a remediation pass; it is recorded as an outstanding item rather than performed here.

tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total arsenic-migration maximum across the material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 3.8 mg/kg for Category I (this row's dry, powder-like and granular fill) and 47 mg/kg for Category III (its fibre wadding, foam slab and discrete pellets), against 25 mg/kg under ASTM F963-17 and 25 mg/kg under NOM-252-SSA1-2011. The Category I value binds at 3.8 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
tAs.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. The register row's own notes record only that the values are unchanged across F963-08/-11/-16/-17/-23. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a figure made mandatory by CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. If ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 / 8.3 is later ingested as a source page that quotes the conformity-decision rule and it does specify a correction, the question may be reopened on that record; until then the stricter figure binds, which is also the position already published on wiki/regulations/astm-f963-soluble-migration and wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. On this row the ASTM and NOM-252 arsenic figures (25 mg/kg) are looser than the binding Category I value of 3.8 mg/kg and do not change the ceiling; they are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family. Arsenic is limited as the TOTAL element by every instrument in the family; inorganic arsenic has no migration counterpart and is handled on the iAs cell. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans two of the Directive's material categories and the stricter of the two is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category III material forms (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling, and the compiled record's candidate set discloses both category values. STRUCTURAL NOTE: the durable fix is to split this row into per-material-category sub-rows, each with its own basis and its own Directive category. That requires new Category 21 subcategory slugs in data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json, which is a Step 0 taxonomy lock and outside a remediation pass; it is recorded as an outstanding item rather than performed here.

iAs.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in loose fill: fibre wadding, foam, granulate, micro-bead, ground shell or bean fill is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
iAs.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (arsenic, total element, both scope tiers), mandatory in Mexico since 2012-08-13. None of the four speciates arsenic.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. loose fill: fibre wadding, foam, granulate, micro-bead, ground shell or bean fill carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, NOM-252-SSA1-2011, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (mercury, total element, both scope tiers). None speciates mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Ni.label: Strictest applicable sovereign nickel-migration maximum across the material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 75 mg/kg for Category I (this row's dry, powder-like and granular fill) and 930 mg/kg for Category III (its fibre wadding, foam slab and discrete pellets). The Category I value binds at 75 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans two of the Directive's material categories and the stricter of the two is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category III material forms (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling, and the compiled record's candidate set discloses both category values. STRUCTURAL NOTE: the durable fix is to split this row into per-material-category sub-rows, each with its own basis and its own Directive category. That requires new Category 21 subcategory slugs in data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json, which is a Step 0 taxonomy lock and outside a remediation pass; it is recorded as an outstanding item rather than performed here.

Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 15 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's dry, powder-like and granular (Category I) material that is 0.9 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.
Sn.basis: element MIGRATION from accessible toy material (EN 71-3, mg/kg of material) — the stricter of the two material-category limit sets this row's scope spans (Category I) is published across the whole row; a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive TOTAL-tin migration maximum, strictest across the Category I (15 000 mg/kg, binding) and Category III (180 000 mg/kg) material forms this row's scope spans, recorded as a SCREEN; the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling for Category I material, 0.9 mg/kg, is a binding parallel obligation pending register ingestion.
Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 0.9 mg/kg for this row's dry, powder-like and granular (Category I) material while this cell publishes 15 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans two of the Directive's material categories and the stricter of the two is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category III material forms (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling, and the compiled record's candidate set discloses both category values. Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.basis: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category I (dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material) value, the stricter of the Category I and Category III values this row's scope spans; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.

Cr.label: Total-chromium migration maximum taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that set one on this basis: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble total chromium 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable total chromium 60 mg/kg for toy or school-article material other than modelling clay and finger paint (MX). Both agree at 60 mg/kg. Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis; ASTM F963-17 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 agree at 60 mg/kg, applied to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. NOM-252's stricter 25 mg/kg tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint; loose toy fill is none of those, so that tier is inapplicable to this row.
